## Site reliability

```{r}
source(here("R", "reliability.R"))
```

Split-half correlations are computed with `split_half_corr()` (see `R/reliability.R`. 

To stablize calculations, correlations are calculated for each of the $\binom{6}{3} / 2 = 10$ splits of the 6 repetitions. For each split, responses are averaged over the repetitions (i.e., 3 per split). Correlations are Fisher z-transformed then averaged (over the 10 split possibilities). The resulting stabilized correlation estimate is then Spearman-Brown corrected. 

Notation: 

- split-half correlation: non-corrected results, interpretable as Pearson's r
- split-half reliability: Spearman-Brown corrected, or $\rho$

Similar to `20260917`, reliabilities were found for

- earlier/median onsets; 
- shorter/longer windows (100 or 150 ms); and 
- none, aggregated, or separated blank images. 

## Correlation

```{r}
#| label: fig-split_corrs_vs
#| fig-cap: "Scatter plots comparing the per-site split-half correlations when onset times are earlier with 100 ms window vs. median with 150 ms window."
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 4.5
regions <- c("V1", "V2", "V4", "IT")
split_corrs <- here(out_dir, "split_corrs.csv") %>%
  read.csv() 

# earlier 100 ms vs. median 150 ms (original)
split_corrs %>%
  filter((onset_type == "earlier" & ms == 100) | (onset_type == "median" & ms == 150)) %>%
  select(-ms) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = onset_type, values_from = corr) %>%
  mutate(region = factor(region, levels = regions)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = median, y = earlier, color = region)) + 
    geom_point() + 
    facet_wrap(vars(region), ncol = 2) +
    labs(x = "Pearson's ρ (median onset, 150 ms)", 
         y = "Pearson's ρ (early onset, 100 ms)") + 
    theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-split_corrs_vs_hist
#| fig-cap: "Histograms comparing the per-site split-half correlations when onset times are earlier with 100 ms window vs. median with 150 ms window."
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 5
library(patchwork)
# earlier 100 ms vs. median 150 ms (original)
split_corrs %>%
  filter((onset_type == "earlier" & ms == 100) | (onset_type == "median" & ms == 150)) %>%
  select(-ms) %>%
  mutate(region = factor(region, levels = regions)) %>%
  mutate(onset_type = replace_when(onset_type, 
    onset_type == "earlier" ~ "Earlier", onset_type == "median" ~ "Median")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = corr, y = ..ncount.., fill = region)) + 
    geom_histogram(bins = 12) + 
    facet_grid(cols = vars(region), rows = vars(onset_type)) +
    labs(x = "Pearson's ρ", 
         y = NULL) + 
    theme(
      legend.position = "none", 
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:5 * 0.2),
      axis.text.y = element_blank(), 
      panel.grid = element_blank())
```

```{r, eval = F}
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 4.5
# earlier 150 ms vs. median 150 ms (original)
split_corrs %>%
  filter(ms == 150) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = onset_type, values_from = corr) %>%
  mutate(region = factor(region, levels = regions)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = median, y = earlier, color = region)) + 
    geom_point() + 
    facet_wrap(vars(region), ncol = 2) +
    labs(x = "Pearson's ρ (median onset, 150 ms)", 
         y = "Pearson's ρ (early onset, 150 ms)") + 
    theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### Comparison of shorter and longer windows

```{r}
#| label: fig-l_windows_vs
#| fig-cap: "Comparison of split-half correlations for windows of 100 ms and windows of 150 ms. In general, split-half correlations are larger for 150 ms windows, with the difference most prominent in earlier onset times."
regions <- c("V1", "V2", "V4", "IT")
split_corrs <- here(out_dir, "split_corrs.csv") %>%
  read.csv() 

# earlier 150 ms vs. earlier 100 ms
split_corrs %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = ms, values_from = corr, names_prefix = "ms_") %>%
  mutate(region = factor(region, levels = regions)) %>%
  mutate(onset_type = replace_when(onset_type, 
    onset_type == "earlier" ~ "Early onset", 
    onset_type == "median" ~ "Median onset")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = ms_150, y = ms_100, color = region)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0) +  
    facet_grid(rows = vars(onset_type), cols = vars(region)) + 
    labs(
      x = "Pearson's r (150 ms)", 
      y = "Pearson's r (100 ms)") + 
    theme(legend.position = "none")
```
## Sparsity estimation

There are two related problems in sparsity estimation:

1. (sparsity inflation) in general, estimates of sparsity will be biased upward; 
2. (sparsity-reliability linkage) due to the dependence of the reliability calculation on variance, the naive estimates of reliability and sparsity are mathematically related. 

Assume a single site. For simplicity, consider the Hoyer sparsity, defined as
$$
S_H = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n} - 1} \left( \sqrt{n} - \frac{\sum_i \mu_i}{\sqrt{\sum_i \mu_i^2}} \right)
$$

**Theorem** (biased sparsity estimation). For true mean responses $\mu_1, \mu_2, \dots, \mu_n$ and observed responses $y_1, y_2, \dots, y_n$ where $\var (y_i) \neq 0$ for any $i$, the $\E [\hat{S}] > S$, i.e., the estimate of sparsity is biased upward. 

*Proof*. One line; follows from Jensen's.
